newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Oct 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Oct 29.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Tuesday:
- Rising oil prices have begun to worry forecasters because they have not retreated as soon as they had expected.
- Cash flow into equity mutual funds is slowing down amid investor nervousness, fewer retirement plan contributions and stock market uncertainty.
- Investors bought up the initial public offering of Russian natural gas company Gazprom.
- Sun Microsystems Inc is to launch on Tuesday its network computer at a lower cost than conventional personal computers.
- Microsoft Corp and Intel Corp announced a strategy to reduce the cost of owning and using a personal computer.
- Calenergy Co Inc of Omaha offered to buy Northern Electric Plc of Britain for $1.23 billion. It plans to present the offer to the company's shareholders.
- New York Stock Exchange wants to expand its trading floor over a street in the city's historic financial district.
- Tandem Computers Inc named Enrico Pesatori as president and chief executive officer.
- Germany's Henkel KGaA made a $1.12 billion offer for Loctite Corp, a specialty chemical maker.
- United Automobile Workers union is continuing its talks with General Motors Corp without calling a strike.
- Merrill Lynch & Co said its president and chief operating officer would become chief executive at the end of the year.
- John Sweeney celebrated his first year as president of the U.S. labor organization AFL-CIO.
